title: Inference Thrift Advisor: continuous workload signatures and safe apply orchestration
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal: Build an 'Inference Thrift Advisor' that synthesizes continuous workload signatures and domain heuristics to recommend batching + caching profiles and perform safe, automated configuration apply/rollback. This ticket covers profiling, signature design, offline simulation, canary & shadow apply orchestration, and telemetry-based rollback rules.

Background: Current autotune/batching components rely on per-workload sampling but lack a compact, stable signature that captures temporal behaviour (arrival rate bursts), context-length distribution, KV cache reuse patterns, presence of function calls/structured outputs, and model variants. Without a robust signature we either over-fit to transient spikes or apply unsafe batch settings that increase tail latency.

Proposal summary:
1) Workload signature: create a deterministic fingerprint that aggregates: model_family, mean+median+90/95/99 context length, inter-arrival-time quantiles, fraction of requests with long prefixes or streaming, KV cache hit ratio, percent of requests using function-calling, and a recent 5-min token-rate trend. The signature should be stable over 10-60 minute windows and include an entropy score to indicate volatility.
2) Offline profiler + cost simulator: extend existing profiler to (a) ingest representative traces, (b) enumerate candidate batching/cache-param combos, (c) simulate expected cost, throughput, and tail latency using sampled kernel profiles and KV cache hit math. Output cost delta, latency delta, and a safety score per candidate.
3) Heuristic recommender: map signatures -> ranked candidate configs using rules plus a small ML scorer (lightweight XGBoost) trained on historical accept/rollback outcomes. Heuristics include: prefer smaller batches for high-entropy signatures, increase cache TTL when prefix reuse > 12%, avoid quantization changes if function-calling rate > 20%.
4) Safe apply orchestration: staged rollout pipeline with shadow apply, canary, incremental ramp, and automated rollback triggers. Integrate with rollout controller in Console: shadow for 24h, canary 1% for 10m, 5% 20m, 25% 1h, 100% only after passing checks.
5) Telemetry & rollback rules: define concrete SLO gates and rollback thresholds (see acceptance_criteria).

Why different: focuses on a compact, entropy-aware 'workload signature' plus an offline cost simulator and ML-scored heuristics to prioritize safe candidate configs. Emphasis on automated safe apply/rollback orchestration integrated with Console and rollout controller, plus explicit shadowing and synthetic evaluation for quality regressions.

Out-of-scope: model quantization kernel work, dedicated cluster autoscaling, private deployment packaging.
acceptance_criteria: Signature schema defined and documented (fields + normalization rules + entropy calculation)
Profiler extension ingests trace files and computes simulated cost/latency per candidate config with <=10% error vs real profile on heldout traces
Heuristic recommender returns top-3 candidate configs with prioritization score and explainability fields
Rollout pipeline implemented: shadow apply -> canary 1% -> staged ramp to 100% with automated rollback controller hooks
Rollback triggers implemented and tested: see rules below; automatic rollback executes within configured M windows
End-to-end integration tests and a runbook updated in Confluence with post-mortem/actions template
rollback_rules: Immediate rollback if request error rate (4xx/5xx) increases by >0.2 percentage points compared to baseline over 5m
Rollback if p99 latency increases by >10% absolute AND p50 increase >15% over baseline within a 30m window
Rollback if conversational-quality regression detected on evaluation prompt set (automated eval score drop >=3 points)
Rollback if KV cache hit ratio drops >12% and tail latency increases
Fail rollout and notify on data plane exceptions during shadow apply

metrics_to_monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency (by model, by rollout cohort)

design_notes: Signature should be both compact (<=256 bytes encoded) and reversible to allow trace-grouping and fast lookup in the recommender DB
Entropy score computed as normalized stddev across recent quantiles; use exponential decay weighting to emphasize recent volatility
Store last-accepted-config per-signature with TTL so recommender can do warm-start suggestions
Shadow apply writes metrics to isolated 'shadow' namespace and must not affect production KV caches or persistent counters
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting to transient bursts -> Mitigation: require stability window and entropy threshold before any production apply
Risk: Recommender causes regressions in hallucination-sensitive routes -> Mitigation: run synthetic eval set during shadow run; block apply on quality regression
Risk: Rollout flaps due to noisy telemetry -> Mitigation: use moving-window aggregation and require multiple consecutive windows to trigger rollback
